correctness.rationale: For a cyclic independent word s of length L=n−1, let a_i=s_i OR s_{i−1} with indices mod L and repeat pair zero at i=L. During the rim sweep the closed count is 2a_i+a_{i+1}+s_i: at the first site the incoming neighbor is the repeated pair, at interior sites it is the already updated predecessor, and at the last the two updated neighbors have bits a_0 and a_1. If a_i=0 then s_i=0, if a_i=1 and s_i=0 the threshold tests a_{i+1}, and if s_i=1 then a_{i+1}=1. Thus the new rim is the shift by one. The degree-one leaf rule is b'_i=a'_i(1−b_i), giving s_{i+1} by cyclic independence. The first L leaf bits show injectivity. All-one rim states retain the rim and complement all leaves; the two families intersect only at the alternating words, two states for even L and none for odd L. The transfer matrix trace is Lucas, including the repetition test at e=1; divisor inversion on fixed words yields primitive orbit counts. Period two in the rotation occurs only at alternation, already counted among the 2^{n−1} leaf-flip orbits. This handles n=3 as well; a single one has exact period L for L≥3. An independent indegree-pruning check confirmed all stated finite recurrent counts at n=3–9, without extrapolating to general n.
residual_risks: The theorem counts the specified invariant union, not all recurrent states; equality in the finite check does not prove all-order exhaustion. No basin or transient claims were validated.
